page: Vultr vhf-6c-24gb is a virtual server belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It features an Intel x86_64 architecture with 6 shared vCPUs, mapped to 3 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The system is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 448 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core and multi-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1540.0 and a multi-core score of 5383.0. Single-threaded gzip compression is a strong point, reaching 33.56 GB/sec. However, memory bandwidth exhibits notable bottlenecks; while cached small-block reads perform at an average 674.29 GB/sec, uncached large-block write bandwidth is poor at 13.1 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the lower tier, with web serving throughput measured at 6.1 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server offers a resource-dense profile for general-purpose workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is suitable for basic web serving, Redis caching, and lightweight application hosting. It is less optimal for memory-intensive database operations, large-scale LLM inference, or heavy multi-threaded decompression tasks due to uncached memory bandwidth constraints and shared CPU limits.
